Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.
Heard Sri Sanjay Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri S.K. Singh, learned AGA for the State.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants to quash the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 675 of 2023 (Rajesh Kumar vs. Abhishek Kumar and others),
under Sections 452, 323, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Bakewar, District Etawah, presently pending in the Court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 4, Etawah as well as summoning order dated 23.05.2024.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that a complaint has been lodged by the opposite party no. 2 on 22.06.2023 against the applicants under Sections 323, 452, 504 and 506(2)
IPC with an allegation that on 13.6.2023 at 06:00 in the evening, when the opposite party no. 2 was with his wife in the house, then the applicants barged into the house and thereafter hurled abuses Abhishek Kumar And 3 Others vs State Of U.P.

sentences.text:
And Another on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122262062/
1 and administered beating, pursuant thereto, the wife of the opposite party no. 2 sustained injuries.
Submission is that the allegations levelled is to get the matter compromise in the pending litigation which happens to be Original Suit No. 131 of 2013.
Post recording of statements under Sections 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C., the applicants have been summoned.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that totally false and frivolous allegations have been levelled without any basis having no nexus with reality particularly when an attempt was made previously also while lodging proceedings in Case Crime No. 06 of 2014, under Sections 376,
354Kha and 506 IPC and in an application under Section 482 No. 24514 of 2023, the applicants have been granted interim protection.
Further submission is that the motivating factor for lodging the criminal proceedings is the pendency of the civil proceedings before the competent court.

5. Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, submits that whatever might be there happens to be an injury report which shows that the incident has occurred wherein the number of the injuries are seven in nature though they are simple and one day old.
6. I have heard these submissions so made across the bar and carefully perused the record.
7. Apparently, proceedings under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. stood lodged by the opposite party no. 2.
Pursuant thereto, the applicants have been summoned.
The statements under Sections 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C. cannot be said to be having any material contradiction or inconsistency.
Moreover, the injury report is already on record.

The contention so raised by the learned counsel for the applicants that the civil proceedings are pending before the competent court of law which became a motivating factor for lodging the present proceedings is concerned, the same may be at best a defence occasion to consider has not arisen till date.
8. Accordingly, no case is made out to interfere.

9. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submits that a protection be accorded to the applicants as non-bailable warrants have been issued and a direction be issued for consideration of bail.
10. Learned A.G.A. has no objection to the same.

11. Considering the submissions raised at the Bar and the statements so sought to be made by them,
the application stands disposed of directing the applicants to appear and surrender before the court below by 20th June, 2025 to obtain bail, then the same shall be decided subject to legal impediment strictly in accordance with the law.
Order Date :- 4.6.2025
